?Neutral Citation No. - 2024:Ahc:150425
Court No. - 71
Case :- Criminal Misc. Bail Cancellation Application No. - 268 of 2024
Applicant :- Smt. Kiran Tomar
Opposite Party :- State of U.P. and Another

Counsel for Applicant :- Ashutosh Mishra,Birendra Singh Khokher
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.,Ishwar Chandra Tyagi
Hon'ble Mayank Kumar Jain,J.

1 . Heard Sri Ashutosh Mishra, learned counsel for the applicant, Sri Ishwar Chandra Tyagi, learned
counsel for the opposite party no.2 and learned Aga for the State.

2. Applicant Kiran Tomar has filed the present Criminal Misc. Bail cancellation application seeking
cancellation of bail granted to opposite party namely Suraj Tomar vide order dated 14.09.2016 by
learned Sessions Judge, Ghaziabad in Case Crime No. 717 of 2016, under Sections 498A, 323, 326,
307 of Ipc relating to Police Station Sihanigate, District Ghaziabad.

3.  Sri Ashutosh Mishra, learned counsel appearing on behalf of applicant submitted that the opposite party no.2 is continuously pressurizing the applicant as well the witnesses of the matter by filing several proceedings against them.
The opposite party no.2 is also misusing the liberty of bail and has filed numerous false cases against them.

After releasing on bail he filed an application under Section 7(1) of Guardian and Wards Act, 1860 before the Principal Judge, Family Court, Ghaziabad Smt. Kiran Tomar vs State Of U.P. And Another on 12 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/22377689/
1 as Case No.49/2016 for the custody of his two daughters.

sentences.text: Thereafter, he filed an application under Section 156(3) Cr.P.C. registered as Case No.1149/2016, under Sections 323, 363, 344, 346, 504 of IPC against applicant and the witnesses of present case having Case Crime No. 717/2016 which was dismissed by the court concerned on 15.12.2016 for default of the applicant.

4. Learned counsel further submitted that opposite party no.2 moved another application before Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Ghaziabad as Complaint No.3294 of 2017 against the witnesses of Case Crime No.717/2016 which was ultimately dismissed by the court concerned on 16.01.2017.
It was observed that averments made by the opposite party no.2 are false and incorrect.
5. It is submitted that the opposite party no.2 lodged another FIR as Crime No.538/2017, under Sections 323, 504, 506, 307, 427 of IPC.
After investigation final report was submitted against Ankur while chargesheet came to be filed against Sudhir Kumar, under Sections 323, 504, 506, 427 of IPC.
The cognizance were taken by the court concerned.

An application under Section 482 Cr.P.C.
was filed by Sudhir Kumar challenging the chargesheet dated 11.05.2017.
This Court vide order dated 08.02.2024 has stayed the proceedings in such cases.

On 12.04.2017 Sudhir Kumar, the brother of the applicant witness in Case Crime No.717 of 2016 was caught hold by opposite party no.2 along with his driver and started beating him inside the premises of Ghaziabad Court.
FIR as Crime No.539 of 2017 under Sections 323, 392 of IPC was lodged against opposite party no.2 and his driver Monu and after investigation charge sheet came to be filed.

6. It is further submitted by learned counsel for the applicant that the opposite party no.2 filed another Complaint numbered as 3293 of 2017 against Sudhir Kumar and Ankur, the witnesses in Case Crime No.717/2016 before A.C.J.M. Court No.3 Ghaziabad under Section 500 of IPC and summons were issued.
Both witnesses have filed application under Section 482 Cr.P.C. in which order for no coercive action has been passed.
Discharge application filed by Sudhir Kumar was dismissed.
Another Application under Section 482 Cr.P.C. was filed before this Court but it was dismissed.
The order of the High Court was challenged before Hon'ble Apex Court and vide order dated 03.03.2023 further proceedings are stayed.

Monu @ Monendra, the driver of opposite party no.2 filed FIR as Crime No.580 of 2018 at Police Station Kavinagar, Ghaziabad under Section 323,
504, 506 and 325 of IPC against Sudhir Kumar.
After investigation, final report was submitted.
Protest petition was filed by informant which was treated as complaint case.

After recording the primary evidence, summoning order was passed on 29.01.2020 which was challenged under the proceedings filed before this Court through an application u/s 482 No.2865/2021 in which protection has been granted.
The stay could not be extended.
An SLP was filed before Hon'ble Apex Court and the stay was extended till further orders.

7. Learned counsel further submitted that Monu @ Munendra filed another FIR as Crime No.910 of 2018 at Police Station Khurja Nagar, District Bulandshahr, under Section 452, 323, 504, 506 of IPC against Sudhir Kumar.
After investigation final report was submitted.
Protest petition was filed by the informant which was treated as a complaint case.
After primary evidence summoning order was passed on 27.02.2023.
The said order was challenged before this Court by filing an application under Section 482 No.1091 of 2024 (Sudhir Vs. State of U.P.) in which protection has been granted vide order dated 03.04.2024.

Applicant filed FIR as Case Crime No.126/2019, Police Station Smt. Kiran Tomar vs State Of U.P. And Another on 12 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/22377689/
2 Surajpur, District Gautambuddh Nagar under Sections 354A, 504, 506 of IPC thereafter, charge sheet came to be filed under Sections 354A, 504, 506 of IPC against opposite party Suraj Tomar,
Gajendra and Monu in which cognizance was taken which was challenged by accused persons through an application u/s 482 Cr.P.C. numbered as 30462 of 2023 which is pending.

However,
opposite party no.2 lodged another FIR having Case Crime No.887/2019, Police Station Kabir Nagar under Sections 307, 504 of IPC against Sudhir and Ankur.
After investigation final report was submitted.
A protest petition was filed by the informant of that case which was treated as complaint case numbered as 5140/2023.
After recording primary evidence summons were issued.
The aforesaid proceedings were challenged through an Application u/s 482 No.8234/2024 in which vide order dated 16.05.2024 a protection was granted.
Applicant lodged another FIR as Crime No.909/2019 under Section 307, 323, 504, 506 of IPC at Police Station Kavi Nagar, District Ghaziabad against opposite party no.2 and his driver Monu.

sentences.text: After investigation charge sheet came to be filed.

Out of frustration and due to anger the opposite party no.2 filed a Complaint No.10137/2019 under Sections 420, 120B, 379 and 411 of IPC and Sections 43, 46, and 72A of IT Act against the Investigating Officer.
Vide order dated 09.06.2022 the said complaint was dismissed.

8. It is submitted that applicant had strong apprehension that the opposite party no.2 can cause irreparable injury to her and her witnesses Sudhir Kumar and Ankur so that they could not testify before the Court in Case No.717/2016 under Sections 498-A, 323, 326, 307 of IPC.

The opposite party no.2 is using the law as a tool to pressurize the applicant to take back the case and the brother of applicant namely Sudhir and Ankur to not give evidence before the Court concerned.
The opposite party no.2 is tempering with the evidence, pressurizing the witnesses.
Thus, the opposite party no.2 is misusing the liberty of bail granted by learned Sessions Judge, Ghaziabad.
9. Per-contra, Sri Ishwar Chandra Tyagi, learned counsel for the opposite party no.2 submitted that all the cases filed by applicant Kiran Tomar are false and frivolous.
The applicant is married with the opposite party no.2 on 15.12.2003.
Some matrimonial disputes arose between them and litigation started to take place.

It is submitted that almost 30 proceedings were initiated/pending/disposed of,
which were filed by applicant Kiran Tomar and her brother against opposite party no.2 and his family.
It is submitted that in none of the cases opposite party no.2 was convicted.

10. It is also submitted that no material is brought on record which demonstrates that the legal proceedings initiated by the opposite party no.2 were initiated to temper the evidence or to pressurize the applicant for compromise in several matters.
The opposite party no.2 has not misused the liberty of bail.
The opposite party no.2 is regularly attending the proceedings and co-operating with the trial.
The opposite party no.2 did not make any inducement or pressure to the applicant or witnesses of the matters, therefore, the bail cancellation application is liable to be rejected.
11. Perused the record.

12. Section 439 (2) of Code Of Criminal Procedure, 1973 provides :-
"(2) A High Court or Court of Session may direct that any person who has been released on bail under this Chapter be arrested and commit him to custody."

The Hon'ble Apex Court in Deepak Yadav VS. State of U.P. & Anr., 2022 (8) SCC 559 referred the grounds for cancellation of bail as laid down by the two Judge bench in Dolat Ram And Others Vs.
State of Haryana, (1995) 1 SCC 349 :
"(i) interference or attempt to interfere with the due course of administration of Justice (ii) evasion or attempt to evade the due course of justice (iii) abuse of the concession granted to the accused in any manner (iv) Possibility of accused absconding (v) Likelihood of/actual misuse of bail (vi) Likelihood of the accused tampering with the evidence or threatening witnesses."

sentences.text:
14. Based on the above grounds, the Hon'ble Apex Court in Deepak Yadav (supra) further observed that:
"33.
It is no doubt true that cancellation of bail cannot be limited to the occurrence of supervening circumstances.
This Court certainly has the inherent powers and discretion to cancel the bail of an accused even in the absence of supervening circumstances.

Following are the illustrative circumstances where the bail can be cancelled :-
33.1
Where the court granting bail takes into account irrelevant material of substantial nature and not trivial nature while ignoring relevant material on record.

33.2 Where the court granting bail overlooks the influential position of the accused in comparison to the victim of abuse or the witnesses especially when there is prima facie misuse of position and power over the victim.
33.3 Where the past criminal record and conduct of the accused is completely ignored while granting bail.
33.4 Where bail has been granted on untenable grounds.
33.5 Where serious discrepancies are found in the order granting bail thereby causing prejudice to justice.
33.6 Where the grant of bail was not appropriate in the first place given the very serious nature of the charges against the accused which disentitles him for bail and thus cannot be justified.

Smt. Kiran Tomar vs State Of U.P. And Another on 12 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/22377689/
4 33.7

sentences.text: When the order granting bail is apparently whimsical, capricious and perverse in the facts of the given case."
15. Admittedly, applicant and opposite party no.2 are wife and husband.
The factum of marriage is admitted to them.
It appears that after sometime some matrimonial disputes arose between applicant and opposite party no.2 and both sides started filing legal proceedings against each other.

16. The applicant did not produce any evidence which can demonstrate that opposite party no.2 initiated legal proceedings against the applicant to pressurize her for amicable settlement in the legal proceedings or to temper the evidence.
It appears to be mere suspicion of the applicant which lead to file the present bail cancellation application.
It is to be noted that applicant herself has also initiated number of legal proceedings against opposite party no.2.
All the proceedings are either pending or stayed by the courts or protection has been granted to the parties concerned.

17. In view of above, present bail cancellation application is devoid of merits and is accodingly,
dismissed.
Order Date :- 12.9.2024
